chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shaybah al-Zuhri, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he said:

Woe to the one who does not submit to Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil. He said: Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' will not enter the heavenly realms until his statement is completed with righteous action. And one who submits to Allah without following a just Imam has no religion; and one who submits to Allah yet obeys an unjust person has no religion. He also said: All communities were deluded by mutual boasting [about quantity], until they visited the graves. He said: One who does good and does not sin is better than one who does good and also sins. And one who does good and sins is better than one who only sins and does no good. He said: Stopping when in doubt is better than plunging into destruction.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between faith, righteous action, and the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Ahwazi’s *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia doctrine that valid submission to God is inextricably linked to adherence to a just Imam (*Imam al-Adl*), distinguishing it from mere obedience to tyrants. It further clarifies the hierarchy of moral states, asserting that consistent virtue outweighs mixed conduct, and establishes the principle of *tawaqquf* (holding back) in matters of doubt as a safeguard against spiritual ruin.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 18.ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, from Abū Shaybah al-Zuhrī, from one of the two [Imams] (a) who said,

“Woe be to the one who does not obey Allah through enjoining good and forbidding evil.” He [further] said, “Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ will never go through the heavenly realms until his statement is complemented with righteous action. And one who submits to Allah without following a just Imām has no religion; and one who submits to Allah yet obeys an unjust person has no religion.” He [also] said, “All communities were deluded by seeking more [of this world than others], until they visited the graves.” He [further] said, “One who does good and does not sin is better than one who does good and [also] sins. And one who does good and sins is better than one who [only] sins and does no good.” And he said, “Stopping when in doubt is better than plunging into destruction.”
